name: Ca2+ entry and [Ca2+]i rise (L-type VGCC, TRPC1, store release)
driver: E (likely) at 50/60 Hz; separate B route for static fields
driver_note: The cleanest B-versus-E test (Liburdy 1992, thymocytes) held B at 22 mT, 60 Hz and found the Ca response followed induced E (1.7 mV/cm, 8.3 T/s computed; implied ring radius 4.1 cm); a pure 60 Hz E field of equal strength gave the same change. Walleczek (3 Hz pulses, 0-28 mT) cannot discriminate because E scaled with B. Static fields (dB/dt = 0) also move Ca influx at 0.6-6 mT plateau (Fanelli) so a B route exists, but one cell-free CaM replication failed.

dBdt_Ts.basis: computed (sine peak assumption; Petecchia is 2 mT / 1.3 ms crude ramp)

E_Vm.basis: reported (1.7 mV/cm, 0.69 mV/cm converted to V/m)

windows.gating: Only activated or challenged cells respond; sign (inhibit or stimulate) depends on activation state.

evidence: in vitro; positive studies single-lab; three null replications (Wey 2000, Lyle 1997, Coulton 1993)
caveat: Walleczek 6.5 mT reduced ConA-induced 45Ca uptake by 45 % (inhibition, not stimulation). Ghibelli used an NMR device (1 T static plus RF), so dB/dt was not zero. BAPTA blocks more completely than nifedipine and some Ca rise survives Ca-free medium, so store release contributes; this is not a VGCC-only story. Lindstrom threshold was not reproduced and the two positive lymphocyte studies imply dB/dt values two to three orders of magnitude apart (176-640x), so no common threshold exists.

name: Ca2+/calmodulin binding (Pilla first-messenger model)
driver: timing / spectral match to binding kinetics; amplitude secondary
driver_note: Pulse duration or carrier period shorter than the bound-Ca2+ lifetime accelerates binding above thermal noise; burst width is the tuning variable. Pilla 1999 retuned the burst and matched effect with 10x lower peak, about 800x lower average amplitude, about 1e6 x lower average power. Independent cell-free tests conflict (Coulton 2000 could not reproduce; Liboff 2003 found a CaM-dependent PDE effect at 20 uT static).

windows.note: Burst width, carrier frequency, B, dB/dt and the CaM binding time constant are not in the retrieved abstracts; none supplied from memory.

evidence: in vitro and rabbit fracture, originating lab
caveat: Muehsam & Pilla 2009 refit older ion-parametric-resonance data to Mg2+ rather than Ca2+, weakening Ca/CaM specificity.

name: eNOS / nitric oxide / cGMP
driver_note: No retrieved study varies B, dB/dt and frequency independently for NO. Peng 2020 compared 1.5 mT/15 Hz with 3.0 mT/30 Hz: both raised p-eNOS (S1177), so the eNOS threshold is at or below 1.5 mT/15 Hz, while only 30 Hz/3.0 mT improved cardiac function.

NO_change.fibroblast: about 2-fold in 15 min, blocked by W-7

windows.schedule: 20 min every 4 h and 15 min every 2 h worked; 5 min every 20 min did not (non-randomised, historical sham; Taylor 2014)
windows.vasodilation: arteriole 26.4 -> 29.1 um (+10.2 %, p<0.01), RBC velocity +5.5 %, abolished by L-NAME (Bragin 2014)
windows.clinical_pain: Heden 2008 VAS fell about 3x faster; Rohde 2010 -57 % at 1 h, IL-1b 275 % lower

evidence: in vitro, animal and small double-blind RCTs, mostly one network
confidence: moderate that NO participates, low for numbers
caveat: Bragin: effect present in the first hours but not significant by 3 h. Nakayama 2016: 0.5 mT, 50 Hz for 24 h did not change NO in RAW264 without LPS, so field effects need a challenge. Taylor 2014 mechanism (PDE feedback) is a hypothesis with no cGMP data.

name: cAMP / PKA / CREB
driver: unresolved; sign depends on tissue and agonist
driver_note: Reduced PTH-stimulated cAMP at induced E <= 1 mV/cm (Luben); raised cAMP at 0.6 mT/50 Hz and 2 mT/15 Hz in osteoblasts via the cilium and sAC; Schnoke found CREB and ERK not activated by PEMF.
caveat: Farndale 1985 did not measure cAMP; the abstract proposes a cAMP mechanism as a hypothesis (collagen rose, proliferation unchanged, temperature rise below 0.1 C).

name: Ion cyclotron / ion parametric resonance and Ca efflux windows
driver: B_AC/B_DC ratio and f vs B_DC (not dB/dt)
driver_note: Resonance condition f_c = qB/2 pi m (Ca2+ 0.766 Hz per uT; 17.9 Hz at 23.4 uT; 38.3 Hz at 50 uT). Yost & Liburdy: 16 Hz, 42.1 uT AC plus 23.4 uT DC inhibited Ca influx and neither field alone did. Zhadin kept the same behavioural effect when DC and AC rose 10x together (dB/dt about 100x), arguing against a dB/dt threshold for this class. Blackman: +/-10 % frequency bandwidth around H+ resonance (45 Hz at 2.97 uT).

windows.bawin: efflux -12 to -15 % at 6 and 16 Hz; thresholds about 10 V/m (chick) and 56 V/m (cat) in air; tissue gradient about 0.1 uV/cm (authors estimate)

evidence: in vitro and rodent, mixed replication
confidence: speculative to low as a therapeutic dose rule; low as a laboratory effect
caveat: Coulton & Barker 1993 saw no [Ca]i change at 16 and 50 Hz with DC shifted up to 25 % either side of resonance. Fields are microtesla, with induced E far below the PEMF range; no pain or bone RCT in the retrieved set uses ICR settings. Adey 1982 "0.96" is a confidence level (about p=0.04), not a p value.

name: VGCC voltage-sensor hypothesis (Pall)
driver: unresolved (claimed field amplitude or pulse shape)
driver_note: 23 studies in which VGCC blockers lower or block EMF effects (Pall 2013 table has no exposure values, so no threshold can be taken from it). Primary data: nifedipine or verapamil reduced effects in four independent labs, but BAPTA did more, Ca-free medium did not abolish the response, and TRPC1 (not L-type) was the entry route in myoblasts.

windows.note: no extractable amplitude or frequency window

confidence: moderate that L-type VGCC contributes in some cell types; low that it is the primary transducer
caveat: Same author argues static fields also act through VGCC, which conflicts with a pure dB/dt story. Later advocacy reviews contain claims not supported by their abstracts.
